title: Boundary Handling
text: Standard LOWESS neighbourhoods become asymmetric boundaries: fewer points exist one side, pulling local fit toward data interior. boundary_policy parameter controls data padded mitigate effect.

title: Boundary Handling

title: LOWESS Concepts
text: LOWESS (Locally Weighted Scatterplot Smoothing) nonparametric regression method fits smooth curves scatter plots without assuming global functional form. Unlike parametric methods (linear regression, polynomial fitting), LOWESS adapts locally data structure, making ideal : Exploratory data analysis — Discover patterns without assumptions Trend estimation — Extract signals noisy time series Baseline correction — Remove systematic effects spectroscopy Genomic smoothing — Smooth methylation, ChIP-seq, expression data

title: LOWESS Concepts
text: point data, LOWESS: Selects neighbors — Choose nearest points (controlled fraction) Assigns weights — Closer points get higher weights (using kernel function) Fits locally — Perform weighted least squares regression Extracts value — Use fitted value smoothed estimate Iterates (optional) — Reweight points based residuals reduce outlier influence

title: Custom Weights
text: Standard LOWESS assigns equal prior trust observations. Custom weights let override assumption point point — distance robustness weighting applied. effective weight observation jj local fit centred xix_i : wij=custom_weights[j]×K(dijhi)×rjw_{ij} = \text{custom\_weights}[j] \times K\!\left(\frac{d_{ij}}{h_i}\right) \times r_j KK distance kernel, hih_i local bandwidth, rjr_j robustness weight current iteration. Batch adapter : custom_weights applies Batch mode. silently ignored Streaming Online adapters.

title: Custom Weights
text: mechanisms handle unreliable data, serve different purposes: compose: can use simultaneously. Custom weights suppress priori bad points; robustness iterations handle residual outliers remain.

title: Custom Weights
text: Set weight 0 bad point — excluded every local fit otherwise include .
code: library(rfastlowess)  x <- 1:10 y <- x * 2.0 y[6] <- 100.0              # spike at index 6  weights <- rep(1.0, 10) weights[6] <- 0.0          # exclude the spike  model <- Lowess(fraction = 0.5, iterations = 0L) result <- fit(model, x, y, custom_weights = weights) cat("Smoothed y[0]:", result$y[1], "\n") #> Smoothed y[0]: 2.572621

title: Custom Weights
text: observation known standard deviation σi\sigma_i, set wi=1/σi2w_i = 1 / \sigma_i^2 give fit information-theoretically optimal weighting.
code: library(rfastlowess) x <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100) y <- sin(x) + 0.1 sigma <- 0.1 + (seq_along(x) %% 4) * 0.1  weights <- 1 / sigma^2 model <- Lowess(fraction = 0.5) result <- fit(model, x, y, custom_weights = weights)  plot(x, y, pch = 16, cex = 0.5 + weights / max(weights),     col = "gray", main = "Inverse-Variance Weighted LOWESS") lines(result$x, result$y, col = "blue", lwd = 2) cat("Smoothed y[0]:", result$y[1], "\n") #> Smoothed y[0]: 0.1922027

title: GPU Backend
text: batch Lowess type can execute GPU-accelerated backend powered wgpu (Vulkan / Metal / DX12). GPU backend reimplements almost entire LOWESS pipeline — local regression fitting, robustness iterations, interval bounds, cross-validation — compute shaders, anchor points fitted parallel. Batch . GPU support applies batch Lowess type . StreamingLowess OnlineLowess remain CPU-. GPU acceleration worth enabling roughly 10K+ points. smaller inputs CPU backend (optionally parallel = TRUE) typically faster GPU dispatch overhead accounted .

title: GPU Backend
text: GPU support opt-included standard CRAN / R-universe builds. Install one-time download: install_gpu() downloads prebuilt GPU-enabled library gpu-builds release — single perpetual release holding GPU artifacts every version, individual version release pages stay uncluttered — copies installed package’s libs/ directory. Restart R installation. Alternatively, build source GPU support:
code: library(rfastlowess)  install_gpu()          # interactive — prompts for confirmation install_gpu(yes = TRUE) # non-interactive make -f bindings/r/Makefile WITH_GPU=1

text: Estimate uncertainty smoothed curve .
code: library(rfastlowess) set.seed(42) x <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100) y <- sin(x) + rnorm(100, sd = 0.3)  model <- Lowess(fraction = 0.5, confidence_intervals = 0.95) result <- fit(model, x, y)  # Plot with bands plot(x, y, pch = 16, col = "gray",     main = "LOWESS with 95% Confidence Intervals") lines(result$x, result$y, col = "blue", lwd = 2) lines(result$x, result$confidence_lower, col = "blue", lty = 2) lines(result$x, result$confidence_upper, col = "blue", lty = 2) cat("95% CI at midpoint: [", result$confidence_lower[50], ", ",     result$confidence_upper[50], "]\n") #> 95% CI at midpoint: [ -0.04604079 ,  0.1249563 ]

title: Weight Functions (Kernels)
text: Cleveland’s original choice. Best -around performance. w(u)=(1−|u|3)3w(u) = (1 - |u|^3)^3 Use : Default choice applications.
code: library(rfastlowess) set.seed(42) x <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100) y <- sin(x) + rnorm(100, sd = 0.3)  model <- Lowess(weight_function = "tricube") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("Smoothed y[0]:", result$y[1], "\n") #> Smoothed y[0]: 0.4862648

title: Weight Functions (Kernels)
text: Theoretically optimal kernel density estimation. w(u)=34(1−u2)w(u) = \frac{3}{4}(1 - u^2) Use : Optimal MSE properties desired.
code: model <- Lowess(weight_function = "epanechnikov") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("Smoothed y[0]:", result$y[1], "\n") #> Smoothed y[0]: 0.4980927

title: Weight Functions (Kernels)
text: Infinitely smooth. boundary effects. w(u)=exp⁡(−u2/2)w(u) = \exp(-u^2/2) Use : Maximum smoothness needed, computational cost acceptable.
code: model <- Lowess(weight_function = "gaussian") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("Smoothed y[0]:", result$y[1], "\n") #> Smoothed y[0]: 0.5254291

title: Merge Strategies
text: Streaming LOWESS processes data fixed-size chunks configurable overlap. Points inside overlap zone fitted twice — left chunk right chunk. merge_strategy decides two estimates combined.
code: Chunk A:   [=========|=====] Chunk B:            [=====|=========] Overlap:            [=====]                       ↑                  merge_strategy                  applied here

title: Merge Strategies
text: Blends left- right-chunk estimates using distance-based weights. Points closer centre chunk get higher weight. Use : General-purpose streaming; reliable option.
code: library(rfastlowess) set.seed(42) x <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100) y <- sin(x) + rnorm(100, sd = 0.3) x_chunk <- x[seq_len(50)] y_chunk <- y[seq_len(50)]  model <- StreamingLowess(     merge_strategy = "weighted_average",     chunk_size = 5000,     overlap = 500 ) result <- process_chunk(model, x_chunk, y_chunk) cat("First 6 smoothed values (weighted_average strategy):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (weighted_average strategy): print(head(result$y)) #> numeric(0)

title: Merge Strategies
text: Takes arithmetic mean left-chunk right-chunk estimates overlap region. Use : Chunks large overlap region uniform data density.
code: model <- StreamingLowess(     merge_strategy = "average",     chunk_size = 5000,     overlap = 500 ) result <- process_chunk(model, x_chunk, y_chunk) cat("First 6 smoothed values (average strategy):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (average strategy): print(head(result$y)) #> numeric(0)

title: Merge Strategies
text: Uses left-chunk estimate overlap region. Use : left chunk larger context window expected accurate overlap boundary.
code: model <- StreamingLowess(     merge_strategy = "take_first",     chunk_size = 5000,     overlap = 500 ) result <- process_chunk(model, x_chunk, y_chunk) cat("First 6 smoothed values (take_first strategy):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (take_first strategy): print(head(result$y)) #> numeric(0)

title: Merge Strategies
text: Uses right-chunk estimate overlap region. Use : right chunk expected provide better context (e.g., data follows).
code: model <- StreamingLowess(     merge_strategy = "take_last",     chunk_size = 5000,     overlap = 500 ) result <- process_chunk(model, x_chunk, y_chunk) cat("First 6 smoothed values (take_last strategy):\n") #> First 6 smoothed values (take_last strategy): print(head(result$y)) #> numeric(0)

title: Quick Start
text: LOWESS can robustly handle outliers iterative reweighting:
code: library(rfastlowess)  x_out <- seq(1, 6, length.out = 6) y_with_outlier <- c(2.0, 4.0, 6.0, 50.0, 10.0, 12.0)  model <- Lowess(     fraction = 0.7,     iterations = 5,     robustness_method = "bisquare",     return_robustness_weights = TRUE ) result <- fit(model, x_out, y_with_outlier)  # Outliers will have low robustness weights for (i in seq_along(result$robustness_weights)) {     if (result$robustness_weights[i] < 0.5)         cat(sprintf("Point %d is likely an outlier (weight: %.3f)\n",                     i, result$robustness_weights[i])) } #> Point 4 is likely an outlier (weight: 0.000)

title: Robustness
text: Standard LOWESS can biased outliers. Robustness iterations downweight points large residuals: Fit initial LOWESS Compute residuals Assign robustness weights (large residuals → low weight) Refit using combined distance × robustness weights Repeat steps 2–4

title: Robustness
text: Smooth downweighting. Points transition gradually full weight zero. w(u)={(1−u2)2|u|<10|u|≥1w(u) = \begin{cases} (1 - u^2)^2 & |u| < 1 \\ 0 & |u| \geq 1 \end{cases} Use : General purpose, balanced approach.
code: library(rfastlowess) set.seed(42) x <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100) y <- sin(x) + rnorm(100, sd = 0.3)  model <- Lowess(iterations = 3, robustness_method = "bisquare") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("Smoothed y[0]:", result$y[1], "\n") #> Smoothed y[0]: 0.4862648

title: Robustness
text: Linear penalty beyond threshold. Less aggressive Bisquare. w(u)={1|u|≤kk/|u||u|>kw(u) = \begin{cases} 1 & |u| \leq k \\ k/|u| & |u| > k \end{cases} Use : Moderate outliers, want retain influence.
code: model <- Lowess(iterations = 3, robustness_method = "huber") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("Smoothed y[0]:", result$y[1], "\n") #> Smoothed y[0]: 0.4937237

title: Robustness
text: Hard threshold. Points either fully weighted completely excluded. w(u)={1|u|≤k0|u|>kw(u) = \begin{cases} 1 & |u| \leq k \\ 0 & |u| > k \end{cases} Use : Extreme outliers, want binary exclusion.
code: model <- Lowess(iterations = 3, robustness_method = "talwar") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("Smoothed y[0]:", result$y[1], "\n") #> Smoothed y[0]: 0.4606284

title: Scaling Methods
text: iterations > 0, LOWESS computes robustness weights comparing residual current residual scale estimate. scaling_method parameter controls scale measured. robustness weight point ii : wi=B(|ri|6⋅σ̂)w_i = B\!\left(\frac{|r_i|}{6 \cdot \hat{\sigma}}\right) BB bisquare function σ̂\hat{\sigma} scale estimate. larger σ̂\hat{\sigma} makes algorithm tolerant large residuals; smaller one makes aggressive.

title: Scaling Methods
text: σ̂=median(|ri−median(ri)|)\hat{\sigma} = \text{median}(|r_i - \text{median}(r_i)|) First centers residuals median, takes median absolute deviations. Double use median makes highly resistant extreme outliers. standard choice robust regression. Use : Data may contain outliers (default applications).
code: library(rfastlowess) set.seed(42) x <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = 100) y <- sin(x) + rnorm(100, sd = 0.3)  model <- Lowess(iterations = 3, scaling_method = "mad") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("Smoothed y[0]:", result$y[1], "\n") #> Smoothed y[0]: 0.4862648

title: Scaling Methods
text: σ̂=median(|ri|)\hat{\sigma} = \text{median}(|r_i|) Uses uncentered median — unlike MAD subtract residual median first. Still robust (median-based) slightly less resistant MAD residuals systematically shifted. Faster MAD practice requires one partial sort. Use : Speed matters data minimal systematic bias residuals.
code: model <- Lowess(iterations = 3, scaling_method = "mar") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("Smoothed y[0]:", result$y[1], "\n") #> Smoothed y[0]: 0.4870733

title: Scaling Methods
text: σ̂=1n∑|ri|\hat{\sigma} = \frac{1}{n}\sum_i |r_i| Arithmetic mean absolute residuals. Non-robust: single extreme outlier inflates σ̂\hat{\sigma}, causing algorithm -downweight . Fastest compute (sort required). Useful data believed clean speed priority. Use : Clean data outliers; maximum computation speed required.
code: model <- Lowess(iterations = 3, scaling_method = "mean") result <- fit(model, x, y) cat("Smoothed y[0]:", result$y[1], "\n") #> Smoothed y[0]: 0.5023604

title: Use Case: Genomic Data Smoothing
text: small fraction = 0.1 lets LOWESS follow fine-scale spatial structure without smearing transitions methylated unmethylated regions. confidence_intervals = 0.95 produces uncertainty bands naturally widen positions sparser CpG coverage, making low-confidence segments immediately apparent plot.
code: library(rfastlowess)  positions <- seq(0, 99000, by = 1000) observed <- 50 + sin(positions / 1000) * 20 + 5  # positions and observed are your methylation data model <- Lowess(     fraction = 0.1,     iterations = 3,     confidence_intervals = 0.95 ) result <- fit(model, positions, observed)  # Smoothed profile in result$y # CI bounds in result$confidence_lower/upper plot(positions, observed, pch = ".", col = "gray",     xlab = "Genomic Position (bp)", ylab = "Methylation Level",     main = "Methylation Profile Smoothing") lines(result$x, result$y, col = "blue", lwd = 2) lines(result$x, result$confidence_lower, col = "blue", lty = 2) lines(result$x, result$confidence_upper, col = "blue", lty = 2) legend("topright", c("Observed", "Smoothed", "95% CI"),         pch = c(1, NA, NA), lty = c(NA, 1, 2),         col = c("gray", "blue", "blue")) cat(sprintf(     "95%% CI: [%.4f, %.4f]\n",     result$confidence_lower[1], result$confidence_upper[1] )) #> 95% CI: [51.6773, 68.7372]

text: true real-time applications point must processed immediately. window_capacity = 25 limits internal buffer 25 recent observations; add_point() call costs O(window) rather growing total history. min_points = 5 suppresses output window holds enough points stable fit — calls made threshold return NULL. update_mode = "incremental" re-fits recent point rather full window, halving typical latency modest accuracy cost.

title: Use Case: Real-Time Processing
text: dashboard pattern uses plain LOWESS fit manually managed sliding window rather OnlineLowess. simplest approach UI framework already owns data buffer need recent smoothed value per frame. trade-full O(window^2) refit every tick; high-frequency streams prefer OnlineLowess update_mode = "incremental" bound per-frame cost.
code: library(rfastlowess)  n <- 100 x <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = n) y <- sin(x) + 0.1  window_x <- numeric(0) window_y <- numeric(0) last_smoothed <- 0  for (i in seq_along(x)) {     window_x <- c(window_x, x[i])     window_y <- c(window_y, y[i])      if (length(window_x) > 50) {         window_x <- window_x[-1]         window_y <- window_y[-1]     }      if (length(window_x) < 2) next     model <- Lowess(fraction = 0.4)     result <- fit(model, window_x, window_y)     last_smoothed <- result$y[length(result$y)] } cat(sprintf("Smoothed (dashboard, latest tick): %.4f\n", last_smoothed)) #> Smoothed (dashboard, latest tick): -0.0663

title: Use Case: Time Series Analysis
text: Remove trend analyze residual patterns. Setting return_residuals = TRUE stores observed - smoothed alongside smooth. slightly wider fraction = 0.3 produces smoother baseline trend, short-duration oscillations end residuals rather absorbed trend component. residual series ready spectral analysis, seasonality detection, change-point methods.

title: Use Case: Time Series Analysis
text: LOWESS naturally handles irregular time sampling:
code: library(rfastlowess)  t_irregular <- vapply(     0:99, function(i) i * 1.0 + (i * 31 %% 10) * 0.1, numeric(1) ) y_irregular <- 10 + 0.3 * t_irregular + 2.0 * sin(t_irregular * 0.1)  # No special handling needed for irregular spacing model <- Lowess(fraction = 0.2) result <- fit(model, t_irregular, y_irregular) cat(sprintf("y[0]: %.4f\n", result$y[1])) #> y[0]: 11.4324

title: Use Case: Time Series Analysis
text: Use different fractions extract features different scales:
code: library(rfastlowess)  n <- 100 t <- seq(0, 2 * pi, length.out = n) y <- sin(t) + 0.1  scales <- c(0.05, 0.2, 0.5) trends <- lapply(scales, function(f) {     model <- Lowess(fraction = f)     fit(model, t, y)$y }) cat("Trend y[0] values:", vapply(trends, function(tr) tr[1], numeric(1)), "\n") #> Trend y[0] values: 0.131712 0.2244466 0.3343704

title: Use Case: Time Series Analysis
text: Biological application:
code: library(rfastlowess)  hours <- seq(0, 24, by = 0.5) i <- seq_along(hours) - 1 expression <- 100 * (1 + 0.5 * sin(hours * pi / 12)) +     ((i * 7 + 3) %% 1.7 - 0.85) * 10  model <- Lowess(     fraction = 0.3,     iterations = 3,     confidence_intervals = 0.95,     return_diagnostics = TRUE ) result <- fit(model, hours, expression) cat(sprintf("R2: %.3f\n", result$diagnostics$r_squared)) #> R2: 0.973
